records.quote: Proposition 1 Let S1, S2, Z be independent random variables with PDFs f1, f2, g respectively. Then the following properties hold: (i) if Z > 0 and S1 ≤st S2, then S1 Z ≤st S2 Z;

records.quote: (ii) if Z > 0 and 0 < s1 ≤ s2 and xg'(x)/g(x) is decreasing in (0, ∞) (8), then s1 Z ≤lr s2 Z;

records.quote: Proposition 2 Let us consider two univariate SN variables such that Zi ∼ SN1(0, 1, αi) for i = 1, 2 with α1 < α2. Then Z1 ≤st Z2.
records.compared: Z1 vs Z2 differing only in shape parameter α

records.quote: Moreover, we have the following property for the st-ordering of univariate SN distributions. This property cannot be extended to the lr order.
records.compared: Z1 vs Z2 with α1 < α2

conclusion.direction: Z1 ≰lr Z2: the st ordering of Proposition 2 does not extend to the lr order

records.ambiguity: Bare prose assertion of non-extension — no formal counterexample or proof printed; recorded as a refutation claim.

note: Both passes agree on Z1 ≤st Z2 (α1<α2). A's extra record reflects a printed prose assertion that the property fails for lr; kept as a refutation record.

records.quote: Proposition 5 Let X1 and X2 be two p-dimensional random vectors such that X1 ∼ STp(ξ1, Ω1, α1, ν1) and X2 ∼ STp(ξ2, Ω2, α2, ν2). If ν1 ≤ ν2 then X2 ≤c−tw X1.
records.family: multivariate skew-t STp(ξ, Ω, α, ν); mixing S = V^{−1/2}, V ∼ χ²ν/ν
records.compared: degrees of freedom ν1 vs ν2 (≤c-tw = Van Zwet convex transform order of quadratic forms, Definition 3)

conclusion.direction: X2 ≤c−tw X1, i.e., Q2 ≤c Q1 — larger ν gives the less tail-weighted vector; c-tw is a total order in the ST family

records.ambiguity: ≤c−tw is the convex transform (Van Zwet) order applied to modular quadratic forms — canonical label 'star' per spec ('star or convex transform'); B's 'cx' label is wrong.

note: Order is the convex-transform order → canonical 'star' (pass A right, B's 'cx' wrong); direction X2 ≤c-tw X1 under ν1 ≤ ν2 as printed.

records.compared: tail weight parameters q1 vs q2

conclusion.direction: X2 ≤c−tw X1, i.e., Q2 ≤c Q1 — larger q gives the less tail-weighted vector; total order in SSL family

records.ambiguity: Same 'star' (convex transform) label correction as Proposition 5.

records.claim: Section 4 application: decade-wise c-tw comparison of ST-fitted maximum temperatures
records.quote: The evolution of extreme episodes along time can be assessed by the estimation of the tail weight parameter ν of the ST model from data for all the decades under consideration. The function selm of the sn R package is used to carry out the estimation. The results ... are shown by the left plot of Fig. 3, which displays the estimations of the tail weight parameter from the first decade (1901−1910) to the last one (2001−2010) for the locations corresponding to the Atlantic, Continental and Mediterranean climate scenarios. It can be observed a decreasing trend along the time, which means that temperatures have evolved towards more extreme summers along time.
records.family: multivariate ST fitted to Iberian Peninsula summer maximum temperatures, 11 decades (1901–1910 to 2001–2010), three climate scenarios
records.compared: decade-wise fitted ST models ordered through estimated ν via Proposition 5

hypotheses.text: ST model fitted per decade; estimated ν decreases along time

conclusion.direction: decreasing ν̂ ⇒ X_earlier ≤c−tw X_later (later decades more tail-weighted / more extreme summers)

records.numbers: ν̂ values only plotted in Fig. 3 (left), not printed numerically; decade range 1901–1910 to 2001–2010
records.ambiguity: Empirical application of Proposition 5 via parameter estimation; conclusion inferred from the plotted decreasing trend of ν̂, no numeric estimates in text.

note: Printed empirical example applying Proposition 5's c-tw ordering to fitted ST models; in scope as an example record.
